CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up after recent hospitalization for fever and elevated white blood cell count.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 39-year-old female with history of quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury. She was admitted to District Regional Hospital on 06/29/2021 and discharged on 07/02/2021. During hospitalization, she presented with spasms, lightheadedness, significant constipation, and diaphoresis. She was febrile with white blood cell count of 23,000. There were concerns for urinary tract infection and she was treated with intravenous antibiotic therapy. She also experienced labile blood pressure, headache, and vomiting. Urine cultures were obtained and reviewed but were described as "not very impressive." Patient believes her symptoms were more likely related to constipation and autonomic dysreflexia rather than a true urinary tract infection. She reports that after discharge, once she had a significant bowel movement at home, she felt much better. She currently denies pain or discomfort and reports feeling back to her normal self. She has a suprapubic catheter. Regarding the timing of hospitalization, patient notes it was very hot during that period in late June.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies pain or discomfort. Denies current spasms, lightheadedness, or constipation issues. Reports feeling back to normal.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Quadriplegia due to prior spinal cord injury
Chronic constipation
Recent hospitalization 06/29/2021-07/02/2021 for fever, elevated WBC, and UTI concerns treated with intravenous antibiotics

MEDICATIONS
Miralax daily for constipation, increases dose when needed
Lactulose for severe constipation (rescue therapy that takes approximately 2 days to work)
Vitamin C taken regularly
Multivitamins

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient tends to stay indoors more during hot weather. Takes vitamin C and multivitamins as supplements. Does not receive annual flu shot. Describes herself as somewhat homeopathic in approach to health. Currently unvaccinated against COVID-19. Has concerns about unknown side effects and reports of "vaccine injury." Believes she is young and healthy enough to withstand COVID-19 even with limited respiratory function. States she is closely monitored.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Auscultated, clear to auscultation with good air movement. Patient able to take deep breaths without difficulty.
Pain: Denies pain or discomfort anywhere.

RESULTS
White blood cell count 23,000 during recent hospitalization (noted to be normal last year)
Urine cultures from recent hospitalization were not impressive

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute to chronic constipation: Patient believes her hospitalization was likely related to dysreflexia from her quadriplegia and constipation rather than true urinary tract infection. Discussed that dehydration from hot weather can worsen constipation. Will continue current bowel regimen with miralax daily and lactulose as rescue for severe constipation. Patient reports good adherence to miralax regimen.

2. Quadriplegia: Continue current management. Patient has suprapubic catheter in place.

3. Leukocytosis: Patient to return in 2 to 3 weeks for fasting labs including complete blood work, CBC with white blood cell count recheck, and complete cholesterol panel. Purpose is to determine if elevated white count normalizes downward or if it remains elevated, which would suggest something else going on with bowels. This appointment will also serve to obtain routine cholesterol labs since patient is due for this screening.

4. COVID-19 vaccine: Patient is currently unvaccinated and expressed hesitancy. Discussed concerns about unknown side effects and vaccine injury. Doctor recommends vaccination given patient's high-risk status due to quadriplegia and respiratory limitation. Discussed vaccine safety and noted that rare side effects like Guillain-Barré syndrome can occur with vaccines but are very rare. Discussed that COVID-19 numbers are currently low and delta variant becomes more contagious but less deadly with mutation. Emphasized that vaccine is the only true preventative mechanism for COVID-19. Patient instructed to think about this decision and contact if she has further questions.
